Then that John,
when he was pressed and did not want to oppose the will of his wife,
referred the matter to her.
She, however, was not willing,
but answered:
"Truly we are obliged to honor him upon our heads,
because he is a great king.
However, for us Syrians {OCR?}, it is not the custom for women to go out into an assembly of men.
Therefore, let him not blame me that I am ashamed to go out."
Then a certain slanderer inflamed the wrath of Khosrow and said to him:
"She despised you, that she did not come out;
and she also said:
'Is this his mind?
Because of this he was cast down from his height.'"
And for this reason he held a grudge against her.
And while the Persians were laying waste to the lands,
Phocas from within was killing the nobles,
until he finished off the freeborn warriors.
Then two powerful patricians, Gregory and Heraclius, were in Africa,
and they came to an agreement with one another,
and sent their sons with armies against Constantinople.
And when the citizens heard, they rejoiced,
and ran out to meet them,
and brought them in with pomp,
and Phocas was killed.
After thirty-two years {OCR?}.
Now when this one reigned, he sent ambassadors to Khosrow, saying:
"Because Phocas killed Maurice, your friend, we killed him."
And with persuasions such as these he hoped that there would be reconciliation.
Khosrow, however, not only was not reconciled,
but added evil to evil.
And in the first year of Heraclius, he conquered Antioch.
And after a year, Bahram, his general, conquered Caesarea of Cappadocia,
and killed myriads in it,
and took captive all of it as booty,
and returned.
And in the fourth year of Heraclius, Rōmīzān, the general who was surnamed Shahrbaraz—
that is to say, 'wild boar'—subjugated
Damascus.
And after a year he took control over Galilee and the region of the Jordan.
And after a year he captured Jerusalem,
and killed in it ninety thousand people.
And at first they made peace with the Jews,
then them too they exiled entirely to Persia.
And in the year after it, Shahrbaraz entered Egypt and conquered it,
and captured Alexandria,
and subjugated Libya as well, up to the border of the Ethiopians.
